To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

''Children's reported fun correlates with specific features of their recorded physiological state during physical play, and these features can be used to build a model of their entertainment preferences that can be used in the design of interactive playgrounds''.

children can report their preferences in terms of fun during physical play, that these preferences correlate with physiological signals, that these preferences can be modeled and that the models can be used to improve the fun in physical play.

the degree of children's entertainment during physical activity is related to the level of their physiological activity and that children's preferences of physical activity can be predicted using physiological measurements.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a methodology to capture and model the affective state during physical game-play, and to provide a real-time feedback to the player that can be used to augment entertainment.
developing a methodology to model children's affective state in physical game play and with identifying the physiological correlates of entertainment.
the development of methods and tools for modeling and augmenting the entertainment experience through the analysis of children's physiological signals during play.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method for entertainment modeling is able to predict the degree to which children enjoy physical games and can therefore serve as a feedback mechanism for entertainment enhancement.

the proposed methodology is able to capture the children's physiological state and to model their entertainment preferences during physical game play, but that the reported entertainment preferences are only a partial indicator of the children's affective state.

, although children do indeed express a strong preference for physical play of low mental and emotional load, they also report as fun games with higher mental and emotional load independently of physical exertion, provided that the game is challenging enough and that the child has the required skills to play it.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reported results provide a solid basis for further research on entertainment augmentation through physiological modeling.
children's physiological signals provide a reliable basis for entertainment modeling, but that the specific features of the signals are highly dependent on the nature of the physical play.
the proposed methodology can be used to construct a model for entertainment that is grounded on children's physiology and is applicable to a variety of physical interactive games.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the physiological state of children during physical game play can be captured by a limited set of features and that these can be used to model the degree to which a game is fun for a given child.
the affective state (entertainment) can be estimated from children's physiological state, and that the affective modeling can be used as a tool to improve the entertainment value of physical games.
it is possible to construct an estimator of the entertainment value of a game based on children's physiological signals.
